items.title: End of an era: Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-B) said Friday that Warren Buffett will step down as chairman, effective immediately, and transition to the role of chairman emeritus. PNC Asset Management Group CIO Amanda Agati and Aptus Capital Advisors Head of Equity and Portfolio Manager David Wagner join Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi to discuss Buffett's departure and his lasting impact on investors.

items.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chair, succeeded by his son
items.summary: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK-A, BRK-B) — to be replaced by his son Howard — after holding the position since 1970. He will be transitioning into a chairman emeritus role. Morning Brief Host Julie Hyman is joined by Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley and Washington Crossing Advisors senior portfolio manager Chad Morganlander to react to this announcement.

items.title: Even as trading and markets moved faster, Warren Buffett made patience profitable and cool
items.summary: Even in the age of algorithms, short attention spans and TikTok teases, Warren Buffett continued to profit with his patient bargain-hunting approach while offering folksy advice on investing and life.  As chairman and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway, Buffett became famous for his unwavering and methodical investing style: Buy good businesses when their prices are low, stay on the sidelines when prices are too high and be patient with well-chosen picks.  The formula of buying good things at low prices sounds simple, and it’s the foundation of a style of investing called “value” hunting.

items.summary: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite rebounded to end Friday’s session slightly higher after spending most of the day in the red.  The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended lower as higher oil prices and bond yields weighed on equities.  Glassmaker  Corning  and optical networking stocks  Coherent  and  Lumentum  rose, while chip manufacturer  Intel  fell 0.2%.
